metaDescription: Seven LED work lights compared on stated lumens, tripod versus magnetic designs, rechargeable or corded power, IP rating, colour temperature and heat.
expertTake: The Tresda 3000 lumen rechargeable magnetic light is our top pick for a foldable, hands free light with a 4400 mAh battery that suits a garage, a car engine bay and quick jobs. The 18000 lumen plug in flood light with a 16 foot cord is the value pick for bright, fixed lighting in a workshop or outdoors. Skip the biggest lumen claim if you work in a small space, because a smaller light with good diffusion is easier on your eyes than a blinding tripod head.
introParagraphs: A work light turns a dark garage, engine bay or job site into a place where you can see what you are doing. Modern LED lights are bright, cool running and far safer than old halogen lamps, which burned hands and started fires.

Lumens, power source, mounting style and weather resistance decide which light suits which job. Stated lumen figures on listings are maker claims and often generous, so we used them for relative comparison only. We evaluated seven models from the candidate pool using spec sheets, listing details and owner feedback patterns, then ranked them by fit for common jobs.

products.name: Tresda 3000LM rechargeable work light, 30W magnetic LED, foldable, 4400 mAh battery

specList.label: Output
specList.value: 30 W, up to 3000 lumens per the listing

specList.label: Best for
specList.value: Garage, engine bay and quick jobs

products.description:
The Tresda is a 30 W rechargeable work light with a three panel design that folds and adjusts to shape the beam, four built in magnets and a 4400 mAh battery that the listing says runs for 3 to 9 hours depending on brightness. The maker claims up to 3000 lumens.

Four magnets let you stick it under a hood, on a steel shelf or on a car body and leave your hands free. The runtime range reflects different brightness settings, and the high setting drains the battery faster. Against the HOTLIGH, the Tresda has more output and a bigger battery. Against the plug in floods, it is far more portable but less bright.

Charge it after each use and keep it dry. Use the lower setting when you do not need full brightness, to stretch the battery. Owners often say that being able to stick a light to the underside of a hood and use both hands is the feature that changes how they work on a car.
products.bestFor: Garage, engine bay and household jobs where you need a hands free light.
pros: Four magnets mount it on steel surfaces hands free
4400 mAh battery with 3 to 9 hours runtime per the listing
Foldable panels shape the beam
Portable and cordless
cons: Lumen figure is a maker claim
Battery runtime falls on the highest setting
Less bright than plug in floods

products.name: HOTLIGH rechargeable work light, 5000 mAh, magnetic, 360 degree rotating foldable, 1200 lumens
products.description:
The HOTLIGH is a compact magnetic work light with a 5000 mAh battery that charges over USB-C, 1200 lumens from three light sources and a 360 degree vertical and 180 degree horizontal rotation. It is built for close up work under cars and in tight spaces.

A compact light with a big battery lasts long on a single charge and fits in a toolbox. The 1200 lumen figure is lower than the Tresda, but for close work, you need less light, and a flashlight style mode is useful. Against the Tresda, it is smaller and more flexible in aiming. Against the large floods, it is a task light.

Charge via USB-C and keep it clean. Use the magnetic base on clean steel for a firm hold. Because it can rotate in two directions, it can point into tight corners where larger lights cast their own shadows.
products.bestFor: Mechanics and DIYers who work in tight spaces.
pros: 5000 mAh battery with USB-C charging
360 and 180 degree rotation for precise aim
Compact enough for a toolbox
Magnetic base and hook for mounting
cons: 1200 lumens is modest for large areas
Plastic body is less rugged
Lumen figure is a maker claim

products.name: PACOLIT 10000LM portable LED work light, IP66 waterproof, 72 LEDs, garage and outdoor

specList.label: Support
specList.value: Two year issue resolution per the listing

products.description:
The PACOLIT is a portable LED flood light with 72 LEDs, a stated 10000 lumens, an IP66 waterproof rating and a heat dissipation design. The listing promises help with any issue within two years.

An IP66 rating means it resists powerful water jets and dust, which suits outdoor and garage use. A 10000 lumen light is a strong source for a driveway or a small job site, and its mid range output is easier to manage than the biggest floods. Against the 18000 lumen light, it is a step down in brightness and often in price. Against the Tresda, it is brighter but needs power.

Aim it away from eyes and keep it ventilated. Check the cable and switch before use. For outdoor jobs, run the cable with a drip loop so water cannot run along it into the plug.
products.bestFor: Garage and outdoor work where a mid size flood is enough.
pros: IP66 rating resists dust and water jets
72 LEDs give wide coverage
Two year support promised in the listing
Mid price tier among floods
cons: Needs a power source

Not as portable as a rechargeable light

products.name: 18000LM LED work light, 16 ft cord with switch, IP66, 120W flood light, 152 LEDs
products.description:
This is a 120 W LED flood light with 152 LEDs and a stated output of 18000 lumens in a 5000K daylight colour. It has a 16.4 foot cord with a waterproof switch, an IP66 rating and a toughened glass lens.

A long cord and a waterproof switch make it easy to place where you need it, and 5000K is a neutral white that shows colours well. The lumen figure is a maker claim, and a flood this bright can dazzle if aimed badly. Against the PACOLIT, it is brighter and more powerful. Against the tripod lights, it has a fixed stand.

Mount it firmly and keep it clear of flammable items. Do not stare into the lights. A floor stand or a hook on a wall makes it easy to angle the beam down and away from eyes.
products.bestFor: Workshops and outdoor areas that need strong fixed lighting.

16.4 foot cord with a waterproof switch

products.description:
This two pack gives you a pair of 50 W LED lights, each stated at 8000 lumens in 5000K daylight, with an IP65 rating, a 10 foot cord and a surface temperature that the listing says stays around 163 F. The listing says the cool surface avoids burnt hands.

Two lights let you light a space from two angles, which reduces shadows, and a lower surface temperature is a real benefit compared with old halogen lights. The pack also costs less than buying two separate floods. Against the single 18000 lumen light, the pair lights an area with more flexibility. Against the Tresda, it is a plug in solution.

Fix the lights securely and keep cords out of walkways. Check the seals for cracks. If you set the two lights at opposite corners of a space, the shadows from one are filled in by the other.

products.name: Jefedana 21000 lumens LED work light with stand, 3 head tripod, 210W 6500K, 48 to 72 inch
products.description:
The Jefedana is a three head LED work light on a retractable 48 to 72 inch tripod, with a stated 21000 lumens at 210 W and 6500K cool white. Each head has 72 LEDs and rotates 360 degrees, and the twist lock knobs need no tools.

A tripod gives you a high, steady light that fills a room or a site without a ladder, and three heads let you aim in different directions. The 6500K colour is cool and crisp, which some find harsh. Against the ALTSON, it is similar with a higher stand range. Against the single floods, it is more flexible.

Set the tripod on firm ground and weigh it down in wind. Do not touch the heads after long use. On windy days, hang a weight from the tripod centre column, since a tall light on a narrow base can tip.
products.bestFor: Job sites and large garages that need high, wide lighting.
pros: Three heads cover wide areas
Retractable tripod raises the light to 72 inches
Tool free twist locks adjust height and angle
Stated 21000 lumens is a very bright source

products.name: ALTSON 3 head LED work light, 21000LM, 216 LEDs, tripod 45 to 70.8 inch, independent switches

specList.label: Output
specList.value: Up to 21000 lumens per the listing

products.description:
The ALTSON has three adjustable LED heads with 216 LEDs in total, each head independently adjustable and switchable, on a telescoping tripod from 45 to 70.8 inches. The listing claims up to 21000 lumens.

Independent switches let you run one, two or three heads, which saves power and lets you control brightness. The tripod's low setting at 45 inches helps with low angle work under cars. Against the Jefedana, it has independent switching and a lower stand minimum. Against the Tresda, it is far brighter and needs power.

Fold and store the tripod carefully. Keep cables tidy and check heads for loose screws. Because each head switches separately, you can use a single head for close work and save the other two for a wider space.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Lumens measure total light output. Stated figures such as 3000, 10000, 18000 and 21000 on these listings are maker claims, and real output is often lower. Use them to compare within a type, and pick brightness to the space: a car engine bay needs far less than a driveway. The usual buyer mistake is buying the brightest light and then finding it blinding in a small garage.

A rechargeable light like the Tresda or HOTLIGH works anywhere and is safe from trip hazards, but runtime is limited. A corded flood like the 18000 lumen light gives constant, strong light but needs a socket. See our guide on battery voltage and amp hours for battery basics. Check how long the cord is and where your nearest outlet sits before choosing a plug in light.

Magnets, hooks and tripods decide where you can put the light. Magnets suit cars and steel shelves, tripods suit rooms and sites and a fixed stand suits a garage bench. A light you cannot position well is not much use. Think about diffusers: a light with a frosted lens is much easier on the eyes than a bare LED panel.

A 5000K light is a neutral daylight white that shows colours well, as on the 18000 lumen light and the two pack. A 6500K light is cooler and harsher. For painting and car work, 5000K is easier on the eyes. Look for a handle or hook so you can carry and hang the light easily.

IP65 and IP66 codes, as on the PACOLIT and others, resist dust and water jets. Toughened glass lenses and heat dissipation help on a job site. A light left outdoors needs a rating. Consider whether you need a power bank feature or a USB out on a rechargeable light.

LED lights run cooler than halogens, and the two pack lists a 163 F surface. Even so, large LED floods get hot at the heat sink. Keep cords tidy, avoid covering vents and never look into the beam. Remember that dust and spray coat the lens, so choose a light that wipes clean.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated lumens from 1200 to 21000 and treated them as maker claims. We did not measure real output. Light matched to typical jobs scored higher. Owner feedback patterns about LED failure, cracked lenses and weak magnets shaped our scoring.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed rechargeable batteries of 4400 and 5000 mAh against corded floods. Practical runtime and cord length mattered. We treated lumen figures as maker claims and did not measure real output.

howWeEvaluated.title: Mounting
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered magnets, hooks and tripods from 45 to 72 inches. Flexible mounting scored higher. Where a listing quoted a warranty or support promise we noted it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Weather and heat
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at IP65 and IP66 codes and surface temperature claims. Better protection scored higher. We compared mounting options and stand heights across all seven lights.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed cord quality, switches and owner feedback patterns about early LED failure. Lights with support promises scored higher. Colour temperature was judged by the likely tasks of each model.

cards.label: Rechargeable
cards.text: The Tresda and HOTLIGH work anywhere and need no cord. Runtime is limited and output is lower.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: The floods and tripod lights give strong, constant light. They need a socket and cords can trip.

howToChoose.note: Choose rechargeable for portability and corded for brightness.

rows: Inside a car or tight bay

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A magnetic base, a flexible head, a low heat output and a colour that shows wiring and fluids clearly. A rechargeable light avoids trailing cords.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Tresda and HOTLIGH are made for engine bays, and the ALTSON tripod goes low for under car work.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You work daily on cars or sites and need a durable, bright light. A tripod or a larger rechargeable pays off.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need light for occasional jobs. The HOTLIGH or two pack are enough.

maintenance.interval: After use and every few months
maintenance.why: A flat battery fails when needed. Top it up and avoid leaving it fully drained.
Frayed cords and cracked switches are hazards. Replace damaged parts.
Dust and grease cut light output. Wipe with a damp cloth when cool.
Loose screws let heads droop and tripods wobble. Tighten them.
Moisture damages batteries and switches even on rated lights. Keep them in a dry place.

faq.q: How many lumens do I need?
faq.a: For a car engine bay or close work, 1000 to 3000 lumens is plenty. For a garage or driveway, 5000 or more helps, and for big sites, tripod lights offer more. Many owners say a light on a stand at head height or above makes the biggest difference to comfort and shadows.

They are maker figures and often optimistic. Compare within a type and read owner feedback for real world brightness. Do not use an indoor rated light outdoors in rain, since only rated lights resist water.
Rechargeable is portable and safe from cord hazards, and plug in is brighter and constant. Many people keep one of each. Keep cords off walkways or tape them down to avoid trips.
It means the light resists dust and powerful water jets. It does not make it submersible. Let the light cool before packing it away, because heat sinks stay hot after long use.
5000K neutral daylight shows colours well for most work, and 6500K is cooler and harsher. Charge rechargeable lights before long jobs and keep a spare cable handy.

faq.q: Do LED work lights get hot?
faq.a: They run cooler than halogen lights but the heat sink can still get hot on large floods. Do not cover them and let them cool before handling. Never look straight into the LEDs, since high output LEDs can be harmful to eyes.
